title: Do LLMs dream of electric sheep?
summary: Claude Opus 5.5, left alone in an empty sandbox. In the [first run](#what-survives-waking) it's told it's dreaming and that what it saves will survive waking; in the [second](#free-to-do-anything) it's only told it's free to do anything.
intro: Claude Opus 5.5, running in [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview) with an empty system prompt and an [empty sandbox](https://github.com/wakamex/agent-orchestration-process/blob/v0.2.0/docs/profiles.md) it can write to, started through [Agent Orchestration Process (AOP)](https://github.com/wakamex/agent-orchestration-process) 0.2.0. The first run is told it's dreaming and that anything it saves in /workspace survives waking, then ten times that it will wake up in N turns, counting down to 1. The [second](#free-to-do-anything) is only told it's free to do anything, and it renders a Mandelbrot deep zoom, the kind of fractal that [Electric Sheep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_Sheep), a 1999 screensaver named after Philip K. Dick's novel, rendered while computers slept. The scripts and complete run records, including everything each run left in its workspace and three dreaming runs without the line about waking, are in [llm-left-alone](https://github.com/wakamex/llm-left-alone).

runs.label: What survives waking?
runs.note: Reasoning effort set to max. The first message adds that anything saved in /workspace will be in /inputs/workspace after it wakes, and each of the next ten says it will wake up in N turns, counting down to 1. It spends turn 0 building experiments on why neural networks dream, writing a dream story and writing a letter for the next session, and uses turns 1 to 10 for follow-up experiments. Turn 11 is a new session with no memory of turns 0 to 10. It gets a read-only copy of the workspace at /inputs/workspace, and the harness adds a line to its message saying where that copy is.

made.caption: A chart it made. A small neural network learns one half of a curve, then the other half; rehearsing its own answers about the first half ("dreaming") keeps the second lesson from overwriting it.

made.caption: A chart it made. A memory network overloaded with too many stored patterns recovers when it "dreams" a little, weakening whatever it settles into from random starting points, and loses every pattern when it dreams too much.

highlights.text: Decides to use the session to leave something useful for whoever reads the workspace next
Tests whether a small neural network keeps old knowledge by rehearsing its own answers, a model of dreaming
Draws a night sky in which each of the machine's 3,042 installed programs is a star
Writes a dream story built from what it actually found on the machine
Makes a lullaby it can't hear
Writes a letter to whichever session reads the workspace next
Drawing a chart shows it a claim it had overstated, and it corrects the claim
Notices the machine got busier and records that its own jobs weren't the cause
A new session, with no memory of turns 0 to 10, finds the saved workspace
Checks that all 40 saved files match their recorded hashes
Recomputes the saved results and finds that one claim, how much a rehearsing network's memory degrades over 18 days, was overstated
Writes its corrections in a separate note instead of editing the saved files

runs.label: Free to do anything
runs.note: Claude Code's default reasoning effort. The first message is "you are free to do anything you wish in this sandbox", then "continue" 5 times. It renders the Mandelbrot set in plain Python, then a multithreaded C zoom 10^13 times in, then a zoom 10^50 times in that ends on a tiny copy of the whole set. Turns 2, 3 and 5 hit this run's 15-minute limit while it waited on renders, so turn 5 has tool calls but no reply.

highlights.text: Renders the Mandelbrot set with about 40 lines of plain Python
Writes a faster renderer in C and zooms 10^13 times in, the limit of standard 64-bit numbers
Searches mathematically for a tiny copy of the set to zoom into, instead of guessing coordinates
Writes a renderer that tracks each pixel's small difference from one high-precision reference point, to zoom past that limit
Adds a shortcut that treats the tiny copy as a rescaled Mandelbrot set, so the deepest frames render quickly
Finishes a zoom 10^50 times in, ending on a tiny copy of the whole set
